reviews.text: I'm sorry but I'm going to refund it for now. I will try it again in the future when there's more content. Right now it's less fun compared to other title from the same genre. The things I dislike : - The meta unlock feels tacked on, there's so few item in the unlock menu and like half of them are minor stuff like X production +10% Y production +10%. Also I think making more stage/level something you need to unlock with the meta currency is a bad decision. It's like you're slowing player progress since player must spent their currency unlocking stage instead of unlocking meta progression. - The dino breeding mechanic is too much of a hassle for the reward it gives, it needs more QoL or more rewarding result for all those micro (Picking male and female dino when your control group lump them into 1 icon is annoying, then if there's a rider on them you need to dismount them, then after you're done with the mating the baby dino need to grow up first, then you need to mount a rider again, way too many hassle for a randomized passive buff. - I can't easily tell the numerical value/stats of my unit or my enemy. This is probably not an issue if you have played a lot but for player who is new to the game it's kinda annoying not being able to easily tell just how strong my unit is or how strong my enemy is The things I like : - The game show you the direction of flyer enemies. Personally I like this even if it makes the difficulty lower. I hate being attacked from blind side by flying unit.

[h2]You Wanna Know If It's Worth It?[/h2] As someone who grew up during the golden age of RTS games, think Red Alert 2, Command & Conquer, Age of Empires, Stronghold, StarCraft, and so many more, that I can't list off the top of my head. I can’t help but get excited when something new tries to capture that magic. Do you remember those endless hours of strategy, challenge, and fun? I sure do. But so few these days know how to recreate it. It's always these long 4X complex monstrocities. Repterra is all of that nostalgia, but with a modern twist: it’s procedurally generated, and it borrows the best elements from the greats. You’ll find classic colony building, resource gathering, production management, hero based RTS, and the ever-present threat of enemy swarms barreling toward your town hall. Massive hordes (like They Are Billions!) keep you on your toes, and you get to fortify your position, manage familiar units, and, yes, tame, raise, and breed dinosaurs. It’s wild, and the action just keeps coming, in all the right ways. Despite the variety, Repterra isn’t bogged down by complexity. It’s accessible but still manages to deliver a serious challenge, from Easy all the way up to Insane. Personally, I managed to scrape a win on Very Hard, but the highest difficulties are brutal, the enemies just don’t go down! Quick thinking, clever rotations, and smart defenses (like using trees for walls) are absolutely essential. If you love classic RTS games and want a fresh challenge, Repterra is absolutely worth checking out. But, while it is almost the perfect title, let's point out some of my concerns. [h2]Issues[/h2] I had a few concerns while playing this game that stood out to me. First, there’s no option to garrison your units inside watch towers or most of the buildings you construct. Strangely, you can put them inside derelict buildings, which feels inconsistent and limits your tactical choices. It would be great to have more control over where my units can take cover, especially in my own structures, which could possibly even increase their own firepower, similar to archer towers in a game like AoEII. On the positive side, being able to have units ride dinosaurs is a fun touch, but it doesn’t fully make up for the lack of garrison options. While you can tame Plesios and other elites, you don't seem to have the ability to Tame the elite pterodactyls. They don't do a whole lot of damage, honestly, so no big deal there. Since it's using the old-style of RTS. You can kite units with the hero, to keep your armies alive as they pick off the strong tanks. Good for helping them promote into higher tiers and fend for themselves, when you unlock the healing passive and such or find a hospital. It's one of those old-quirks that is both a good and bad feature since its a classic gimmick that is a part of hands off strategy and cheese. Another issue is the absence of quick formation tools. You can’t easily organize your units into preset or complex formations. Instead, you have to pause the game and manually position each unit in the desired zones, which becomes tedious, especially when trying to set up elaborate defenses. This limitation makes it nearly impossible to manage large-scale strategies efficiently. As a result, I often had to rely more on sniper and artillery towers for defense, using them as my last line of protection when the walls were breached. It uses a form of Roguelite progression. The more you play, the more things like 10% increase to production and other such values you can unlock, which are limited to a maximum of (4) when you've fully unlocked the full list of perks. Weird, I feel like it defeats the purpose. You don't have to use it, it's just... weird to see it. Like, if you were playing Age of Empires and using the monks to hold onto a relic, it's the joy of searching for them, not having a perk given to you immediately to tell you where it is on the map, before the game even starts. It would be better to have the ability to see all the resource boxes on the map as a research upgrade instead of this out of game feature, in all honesty. Overall, these missing features and weird features made the gameplay feel a bit restrictive. I hope future updates address these areas to give players more tactical flexibility and smoother control over their armies, since this is still n Early Access. Lots of possibilities still to come. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] Repterra manages to balance nostalgia and fresh ideas, offering a top tier experience for strategy fans. While a few things hold it back from being truly great, it’s clear there’s a solid foundation here and plenty of potential. I’m cautiously optimistic about where it could go from here, and for anyone who enjoys this genre, it’s definitely one to keep your eye on. I'm still enjoying every moment, and the more stages I unlock, the more desperately hopeless it seems for my own survival, but that's the best part. This is an incredible game which I believe is done by just one developer and I can tell this developer really cares about his game as he's fairly engaging with his community. If you have played They Are Billions or perhaps Diplomacy is Not an Option, you may very well get an idea what kind of game this is. You will be able to train standard human soldiers or engineers as humans or train dinosaurs as your reptile friends to help you complete your objective which is to survive all the enemy waves and gradually clear the map of hostiles and expand your base. There are some bugs here and there, but I never found anything to major. I feel the game could use more units, especially human ones since the solider is the only combat unit of the human variety other than the occasional shock trooper you might find in a crate. Shock troopers are supposed to be from the 3rd faction coming later in an update though. One faction has a tamer but he doesn't fight but attempts to tame dinosaurs. Most of your variety comes from the dinosaurs instead as you can have riders on certain ones to give them an extra ability, but with more human unit options, we could have more variety me thinks. I feel that there could be tech lvl 1-3 units of both human and dino. One other cool mechanic is being able to breed the dinosaurs, though you can only mate 2 sets of dinos at any given time and their baby will have an extra perk to make them more useful like more health or speed or immunity to taking damage while standing in the green ore that is radiated. There's not much in way of music in the game, but the combat music for the waves is really cool. I am not expecting a lot from a solo developer in this part though I feel like each biome could use its own theme and combat theme for a bit of variety at least. There's plenty of difficulty options and fortunately this is great for newcomers or slower players who had hard time on TAB or any game like it. Overall, I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of the gameplay style and especially if it goes on sale. With some updates and bug fixes, this can be a nice hidden gem.

[h1] 《Repterra》简评[/h1] [h3] 那天晚上，亿万僵尸和红警都喝多了…… [/h3] 《Repterra》是一款以恐龙为主要亮点的基地建设生存即时战略游戏。作为一款像素复古的玩法类似亿万僵尸的基地建设生存rts游戏，巧妙地以恐龙为题材切入，我们得以在这个恐龙横行的世界之中建造基地，部署建筑以及各种防御手段、驯服并繁殖恐龙、建造设施实行基因突变来改造恐龙，在获得更强的恐龙的同时，积极的保护自己的基地免受袭来的恐龙摧毁，获得最终的游戏胜利。 [h3] 核心玩法及亮点 [/h3] 游戏整体的模板可以说与亿万僵尸非常类似，玩起来一样的带劲。而且爽感上也是非常足的，在早些年儿时涉猎过红警，并且在前些年玩过亿万僵尸之后，就一直对这种类型的游戏颇有点情有独钟的味道，也是在看到这款游戏之后，忍不住开始进行游玩。目前来说虽然仍处于ea阶段，但是能看出潜力这一块还是有的，玩起来很舒服而且也够爽。 只能说如果玩过亿万僵尸或者说红警以及类似游戏的玩家而言，掌握这款游戏并不难，上手难度其实不高，不过个人觉得如果是纯新手不沾边的话，还是需要在一开始摸索一下，对新手的引导有点不详尽，但确实挺有趣的，我的家人就是一开始没玩下去，但这几天也是开始上头了，哈哈哈。 前期基本上就是围绕着基地周围做文章，布置各种基础设施，例如建造住房、农场以及各种防御性措施还有造兵设施等等，节奏偏缓，第一波攻击在十五分钟之后开始，这一波次一般运营得当通过是没有什么问题的。而且通过波次之后能对整体以及英雄做出强化。 整体的玩法上其实感觉与亿万僵尸类似，而且整体难度也偏简单化，但是游戏本身确实是有趣的，毕竟题材好，而且恐龙这个背景也挺不错的。 [h3] 短板与可优化部分 [/h3] 游戏的美术这方面确实一般，甚至有点糊糊的。 玩起来挺爽的，但要说实话的话，确实只有恐龙算是特色，希望能在接下来的ea更新路线中推出更具自身特色的设置。 [h3] 总结 [/h3] 总的来说，本作是一款类亿万僵尸的基地建设生存rts游戏，游戏整体的玩法可以算是继承了精华，还是很优秀的，玩起来很爽，虽然说也是存在一定的问题，但总的来说可以一玩。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

A reimagining of the gameplay brought fourth by games like They Are Billions, but instead of Zombies you fight dinosaurs. The dinosaurs are varied enough and offer different strategic approaches, but balancing are still, as of now, in need of some fine-tuning in terms of waves and unit strength. The air and water enemies/units make for an interesting shake-up in your strategy, making simple blockades of trees or body's of water no longer an ultimate defence against the enemy. The units you can train are fun and the breeding mechanic is interesting but I have yet to really care for it, it can definitely be explored further. The different factions you play as have slight differences and as you play you can unlock their perks and make any faction work like another, with the exception of the unique unit. Played 50 hours of the beta, so add that to my playtime, its a great game to play while listening to a podcast or if you're in need of a base builder that will make you work a bit for the rewards. I recommend this game, especially on a sale, IF you are into the RTS+BaseBuilding genre (or like Dinosaurs and want a decent entryway into the genre) The developer(s) are working on this game continuously and I can imagine I will like this game even more in a few months time, but as is right now its a full game worth playing.

It plays a lot like They Are Billions, with more maps and enemies that fly and swim. The Dinos are very tanky on the harder difficulties. You can capture dinos and breed them which is a nice feature to play with. This game is more forgiving than TAB, but still a challenge .

I think at this time it needs a bit more time to work on adding features and trying to make itself different from They Are Billions! outside of a few QoL improvements and I guess dinosaur breeding. For the price you're better off just paying the extra $10 USD and playing Billions until this game either releases or gets more content. The perks you can buy with DNA don't do much, and don't feel as if you're getting real progression for obtaining them. As another review said - it just feels like forced restrictions to make you try and feel as if there is some form of progression in the game. The roguelike is neat for your hero, but outside of that it isn't really that unique of a game. Wait to see what full release brings.

Basically the best age of empires with dinosaurs ever made!! even tho its still in early access, the game already has a lot of content and four different campaign maps. the mechanics and gameplay are very similar to age of empires, you build your city, research upgrades, create armies (made up of both dinosaurs and humans), explore the region for resources and, of course, fight enemies. the biggest difference is that right now theres no kingdom vs kingdom battle mode, which would be the perfect addition and i really hope they add it at some point, bc for me the best part of age of empires has always been those deathmatch style battles between kingdoms, whether against other players or the AI. in repterra that mode doesnt exist yet, theres only the campaign, which is all about building a kingdom from scratch across four different regions, each with its own challenges, adapting to each environment to survive and grow depending on the available resources and unique conditions of every map. from time to time you also have to survive waves of enemy dinosaurs attacking your city from different directions. each map has several waves, ending with the final and most difficult one before you can complete the stage and move on to the next. the biggest issue for me is that you need to earn enough points to unlock the next map, creating a grind system where you have to replay the same maps on higher difficulties to collect enough points. i think it would be much better if all four maps were unlocked from the start, although that would also make the game much shorter since you could finish it in less than 8 hours this way. overall this is a really good and promising game and i hope they improve the point system, add more campaign maps and eventually create a kingdom vs kingdom battle mode like age of empires!!
